title: Cap. X: Martyr answers — limit, permission, Spirit, regenerating grace
pass_a_gloss: To the questioner asking why parents stained with varied sins do not always transmit those stains: Placeus answers with Peter Martyr's words — because God set a limit lest evil rage without bound, and suspended this propagation of evil. Why does disobedient Adam generate sons rebellious to God and stubborn by nature? Because God willed to permit — that is, not to hinder — Adam's fall and the fall's propagation. Why does idolatrous Ahaz not generate a Hezekiah like himself? Because God, who had chosen Hezekiah, freed him from paternal idolatry by the Holy Spirit's power. Why do adulterers, drunkards, and robbers not always beget children plunging into the same vices? Because those vices are either not propagated, God's providence blocking them as it looks to the human race's conservation, or once propagated they are removed by regenerating grace.
pass_b_english: Ask, then, why parents stained by many kinds of sin do not always pass those stains to their children. I answer with Peter Martyr: God fixed a bound so that evil would not rage without measure, and He held this spread of evil in suspension. Why does disobedient Adam still beget sons rebellious toward God and stubborn by nature? Because God willed to permit the fall — which is to say, not to stop Adam's fall or its onward spread. Why does idolatrous Ahaz fail to beget a Hezekiah in his own likeness? Because the God who had chosen Hezekiah loosed him from his father's idolatry by the Holy Spirit's power. And why do adulterers, drunkards, and robbers not always raise children rushing into the same vices? Either providence, watching over the human race's conservation, blocks those vices from spreading, or regenerating grace later strips away what did spread.
source_text: Quaerenti ergo, unde fit, ut parentes, qui peccatis variis sese commaculant, inquinamenta illa peccatorum suorum non semper transmittant in liberos? Respondeo verbis Petri Martyris, quia Deus modum praefixit, ne malum grassetur in immensum, & hanc mali propagationem suspendit. Cur Adamus inobediens filios generat rebelles Deo, & natura contumaces? Respondeo, quia Deus voluit permittere, hoc est, non impedire lapsum Adami & lapsus propagationem. Cur Achas idololatra non generat Ezechiam sibi similem? Quia Deus, qui Ezechiam elegerat, eum a paterna idololatria Spiritus sancti virtute liberavit. Cur adulteri, ebriosi, praedones, non semper gignunt filios in eadem vitia praecipites? Quia vitia illa, vel non propagantur impediente Dei providentia, quae humani generis conservationi prospicit, vel propagata tolluntur regenerationis gratia.

choices.decision: God bounds evil's spread without needing antecedent imputation
election + Spirit frees from paternal idolatry

notes: Cap. X alteram densify §114. Martyr citation for limit on evil's spread.
